rationale: param_efficient-claude-agentic: reg_type=foe, bilateral_on_top=True, proj_filter_on=False, n_iter=5, learnable_alpha=True, alpha_init=0.1, foe_n_filters=24, foe_kernel=7, foe_n_bumps=31, n_bf=3, bf_multiscale=True, bf_sigmas=[0.8, 1.6, 3.2], bf_kernel=7, bf_sigma_r=0.02, bf_gain_init=0.0, epochs=16, cosine_lr=True, lr=0.005, max_train_s=1080, batch_size=4, train_n=200, val_n=200, display_min=0.0, display_max=0.05, seed=42, rationale=iter-7 param_efficient breast -- LEARNED PER-STEP DC WEIGHT (step toward VN). SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: 6 iters map the plain tied-GD unroll. KEY new finding iter-6: deep DC (K20) on the lean prox gave hr 0.0 -- DEEPER DC made it WORSE (0.066->0.0), not better. So the problem is NOT under-consistency: on 128-view sparse data the DC gradient R^T(Rx-g) itself is CORRUPTING -- with only 128 views R^T R is a STREAKY operator, so back-projecting the residual RE-INJECTS coherent streaks; iterating it 20x AMPLIFIES exactly what we want removed. This is why LPD (primal-dual) + VN (learned per-step gradient weighting) win and a plain repeated R^T(Rx-g) GD unroll caps ~image-domain. Best point stays iter-1 0.264 (FoE capacity as image cleanup). (2) FAILURE MODE: raw tied DC gradient amplifies streaks over steps; a SINGLE shared scalar alpha can't attenuate the harmful later steps. (3) ONE KNOB: per_step_alpha False->True on the FoE+bilateral K5 arch (iter-2 base, the fully-trained 0.190 config). +4 params (5 per-step alphas vs 1) -> ~1937 total. This is the MINIMAL move from plain-GD toward VN: each step learns its OWN DC weight, so the net can DOWN-WEIGHT the streak-amplifying later steps. (4) HYPOTHESIS: learned per-step alphas let the unroll learn to apply DC strongly early (coarse consistency) then softly late (avoid streak re-injection), rescuing the fully-trained FoE from the over-regularize/corrupt regime -> hr exceeds 0.264, because per-step DC weighting is VN's core trick and it directly targets the iter-6 corruption finding. (5) BUDGET: K=5 FoE+bilateral, train_n=200, 1080s backstop + 200-val -> <20min (same cost as iter-2). (6) SERIAL; iter-8 self-dispatches (next: if per-step helps, sweep K deeper WITH per-step alphas; if not, projection-domain filter +5p)., per_step_alpha=True
